name: Li Zhenyu
current_role: Co-founder & Chairman, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Li Zhenyu spent 16 years at Baidu (from 2007), rising to senior VP and president of the Intelligent Driving Group, where he led the Apollo autonomous-driving platform and the Apollo Go (Luobo Kuaipao) robotaxi service. He stepped back from IDG in late 2023 and in 2025 co-founded TARS with ex-Huawei executives Chen Yilun and Ding Wenchao; TARS raised a record ~$455M Pre-A in 2026.
interesting_fact: He built Apollo Go (Luobo Kuaipao), described as the world's largest robotaxi platform, before turning to embodied AI.
deep_cut_fact: A Beihang University (BUAA) master's graduate, he began his career doing network-technology R&D at Huawei, where he received Huawei's top honour, before Baidu recruited him in 2007; inside Baidu he was known as the 'firefighting captain' (救火队长).
notes: Only company-level contact found (TARS PR). Low personal public profile outside Chinese media.

name: Kevin Bai
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Slash (San Francisco vertical-banking fintech)
profile: Kevin Bai co-founded Slash with Victor Cardenas around 2021 after dropping out of the University of Waterloo. As CTO he runs the technology behind Slash's industry-specific banking, cards and stablecoin payments platform, built on Column bank; Slash raised a $100M Series C at a $1.4B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Slash scaled to about $150M annualized revenue with only 15 engineers, which Bai wrote about on the company blog.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Thunder Bay, Ontario, and immigrated to the US after dropping out of UWaterloo to work on Slash full time; he also wrote a Slash engineering post on designing a data-correctness verification system.
notes: Don't confuse with other Kevin Bais (e.g. at Anthropic or Rippling). No published personal or press email; Slash lists only support@slash.com.

name: Jairaj Sethi
profile: Jairaj Sethi is a University of Waterloo graduate who was head of platform and principal developer at Kik Interactive (2012-2017) before co-founding Substack in 2017 with Chris Best and Hamish McKenzie. As CTO he leads engineering for the subscription publishing platform, which raised a $100M Series C in 2025.
interesting_fact: He came to Substack from Kik, the Canadian messaging app with hundreds of millions of users, where Hamish McKenzie says he was 'the top developer'.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2020 thank-you note, co-founder Hamish McKenzie wrote that Jairaj 'is driven by data and logic, never taking an assumption for granted (this drives me crazy!)'.
notes: Keeps a low public profile; best route is Substack press or an intro via Hamish McKenzie. Gold House says he has also founded startups in education and mental health and lists him as Toronto-based. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so his personal accounts were not checked.
